questions.question: When should you look into the back of the fifth wheel?

options.text: While testing your air brakes.
If your vehicle begins to skid.
When inspecting a coupling.

questions.correctAnswerText: When inspecting a coupling.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, look under the trailer into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
Make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly.
Hold people responsible for inspecting the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain why you must check the items you are checking.
Change the coolant.
Replace a headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you must check the items you are checking.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete vehicle inspection. You will need to explain what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: Older trailers have no spring brakes. What happens if the air supply leaks away?

options.text: The trailer will stop normally.
The trailer will have no brakes.
The trailer will speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air tank air supply leaks away, the trailer will have no working brakes and the wheels will turn freely.

questions.question: What should you NOT base your decision to shift gears on?

options.text: Your engine speed (rpm).
Your vehicle speed (mph).
The actions of the vehicle next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The actions of the vehicle next to you.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine rpm range and vehicle speed. Do not base your decision on what other vehicles are doing.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?

options.text: An explosive.
Liquid.
Corrosive material.

questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Explosives are classified as Class 1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Why should you do routine vehicle inspections?

options.text: To ensure safety.
To improve gas mileage.
To improve comfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: To ensure safety.
questions.explanation: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle is to keep yourself and other drivers safe.

questions.question: Can you use radial and bias-ply tires together?

options.text: Yes, they can be used together.
Yes, they can be used together on the front.
No, they should not be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they should not be used together.
questions.explanation: Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires. All tires on a vehicle must be the same style and size.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Trouble focusing and blinking frequently.
Yawning often or rubbing your eyes.
Staying in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying in your lane.
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, drifting from your lane, and following too closely. Staying in your lane is safe driving, not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?

options.text: Hoses.
An air compressor.
Air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor.
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving.
Pull over and check what is wrong.
Turn on the air conditioner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, stop driving right away. Look for the problem. Your engine could fail or catch fire if you keep driving.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what will you be asked to do?

options.text: Explain what you inspect and why.
Replace an electrical fuse.
Unload the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must complete a full inspection. You must explain to the examiner what you are checking and why you are checking those items.

questions.question: If you start a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection, what may happen?

options.text: You will likely complete the turn safely.
You may hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
Other drivers will move to let you turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what can a separate air tank be used for?

options.text: Make the air brakes work better.
Temporarily release the spring brakes.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Temporarily release the spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if low air pressure activates them. Pushing the right control releases the spring brakes for a short time. This lets the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving with the intent to harm others
Driving a vehicle that is unsafe
Driving a vehicle that has not been inspected

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving with the intent to harm others
questions.explanation: Road rage means driving with the intent to harm others or to physically attack another driver or their vehicle. This is different from aggressive driving, which is selfish or rude driving behavior.

questions.question: When driving at night, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure you are well rested.
Make sure your glasses are clean.
Wear sunglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear sunglasses.
questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses when driving at night. They reduce your ability to see. If you wear eyeglasses, keep them clean. Make sure you are rested and alert before driving at night.

questions.question: When entering traffic with a double or triple, what should a driver do?

options.text: Assume other drivers will make space for you.
Wait for a gap large enough for your entire vehicle to merge safely.
Decrease your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your entire vehicle to merge safely.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples need more space than other commercial vehicles. Before entering or crossing traffic, make sure there is enough space for your entire vehicle without causing a collision.

questions.question: Where are regrooved tires allowed on a bus?

options.text: Only on the front of a bus.
Only on the rear of a bus.
Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand while the other rests.
With both hands for a firm grip.
Release it if the vehicle approaches a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands for a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before driving.
While driving.
After driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before driving.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before you start driving. Your posture changes from day to day, so your mirrors may need adjustment.
